details:
Dear VRChat Team,

I am a VRChat user from the Chinese‑speaking community, and I am writing to kindly request that you add “Hakka (客家話 / Hakka Chinese)” as a selectable language in the language field on the VRChat.

In recent updates and feedback discussions, VRChat has shown a strong willingness to recognize more Sinitic (Chinese‑family) languages separately, such as Cantonese, Wu, and even Teochew, rather than grouping everything under a single “Chinese” label. This is a very positive step for linguistic diversity and makes many speakers feel that their real everyday language is being respected.

Hakka is one of the major Sinitic languages, with a long history and a very wide geographic distribution. Large Hakka communities are found across southern China (especially Guangdong, Fujian, Jiangxi), in Taiwan, and throughout Southeast Asia, particularly in Malaysia and Singapore. In Taiwan alone, around 4.2 million people self‑identify as Hakka, accounting for about 18% of the population and forming the second‑largest ethnic group; in many townships and districts, Hakka speakers make up more than one‑third of the residents. In Malaysia, Hakka is so widely used that in some regions it functions as the main lingua franca among local Chinese communities.

Given this global spread, Hakka players are already part of the VRChat user base, just like speakers of Cantonese, Wu, and other Chinese varieties that have begun to appear as separate language options. When VRChat recognizes Sinitic languages such as Wu and Cantonese as distinct choices, it sends a strong message that each community’s language and identity matters; by the same logic, it is very natural and fair to also include Hakka, which has millions of speakers and its own rich culture, literature, and media.

In the official VRChat feedback space, users have already successfully requested the addition of specific languages—such as Teochew—to the bio language list, arguing that “we all speak equal languages and have our own groups.” Hakka speakers around the world feel the same way: we would like to be able to list “Hakka” clearly in our profiles, so that other Hakka users can instantly recognize us, connect more easily, and build communities in VRChat just as other language groups do.

For implementation, I would like to propose the following:

1. Language name shown in the list: “Hakka (客家話 / Hakka Chinese)” so that it is clear to both international users and native speakers.

2. Placement: alongside existing Sinitic entries such as “Mandarin Chinese,” “Cantonese,” and “Wu,” keeping the structure consistent.

3. Scope: at minimum, add Hakka to the “Languages I know” field in user bios on the website, which is already used to advertise spoken languages; ideally, mirror this wherever other specific Sinitic languages are presented.

Adding “Hakka (客家話 / Hakka Chinese)” is a relatively small UI change, but it would have a big symbolic impact. It would acknowledge a major world language spoken across China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Singapore, and many other places, and it would help Hakka players feel seen and welcomed in VRChat’s multilingual environment. It would also be consistent with the direction VRChat has already taken in expanding language options and recognizing more varieties requested by the community.

Thank you very much for considering this request and for all the work your team has done to improve localization and language support in VRChat. If you need any additional information, examples, or community feedback from Hakka speakers, I would be very happy to help or to connect you with others who are interested.

Sincerely,

VRChat Username: RyuDensetsu

Location: Taiwan
title: Request to Add “Hakka (客家話 / Hakka Chinese)” as a Language Option in VRChat
